```{=html}
.flow .step:after{content:'→';position:absolute;right:-22px;top:50%;transform:translateY(-50%);color:var(--berry);font-size:18px}
.flow .step:last-child{margin-right:0}.flow .step:last-child:after{display:none}
```

## Overview {.proposal-panel}

My goal is a professional portfolio that brings my digital marketing, creative strategy and marketing analytics work into one place. I want it to show more than final results. Each project page should show how I frame a business problem, work with the data and turn it into a recommendation.

The site will be built in Quarto, kept in a GitHub repo and deployed on Netlify, which rebuilds the site on every push. The site also becomes a data source: GA4 tracks it, and that traffic becomes one of the analytics projects.

## Website structure {.proposal-panel}

Four tabs in the navigation: Home, Digital Marketing Projects, Marketing Analytics Projects and Resume. The GA4 traffic report and the Reveal.js presentation are projects inside Marketing Analytics, not separate tabs.

## Build and tracking workflow {.proposal-panel}

Two workflows run the site. The first publishes it. The second turns its traffic into data for the GA4 report.

```{=html}
<p class="flow-label">Publishing workflow</p>
<div class="flow">
  <div class="step"><b>Write</b><span>Pages and reports as .qmd in Positron</span></div>
  <div class="step"><b>Render</b><span><code>quarto render</code> locally to check pages</span></div>
  <div class="step"><b>Commit</b><span>Push to the GitHub repo</span></div>
  <div class="step"><b>Deploy</b><span>Netlify builds from the repo on every push</span></div>
  <div class="step out"><b>Live site</b><span>Public portfolio link for applications</span></div>
</div>

<p class="flow-label">Tracking and analytics workflow</p>
<div class="flow">
  <div class="step"><b>GA4 tag</b><span>Added to every page through <code>_quarto.yml</code></span></div>
  <div class="step"><b>Search Console</b><span>Verify site, submit sitemap, get indexed</span></div>
  <div class="step"><b>Link GSC → GA4</b><span>Search queries appear next to traffic</span></div>
  <div class="step"><b>BigQuery export</b><span>Daily GA4 event export</span></div>
  <div class="step"><b>Looker Studio</b><span>Traffic and conversion dashboard</span></div>
  <div class="step out"><b>Quarto report</b><span>Insights published as a project page</span></div>
</div>
```

```{=html}
<div class="proj">
  <div class="proj-head"><div><div class="where">Digital Marketing · Project 1</div><h4>GA4 Channel Performance and Marketing Strategy</h4></div><div class="tags"><i>GA4</i><i>Descriptive analytics</i><i>Channel strategy</i></div></div>
  <div class="proj-body">
    <div class="facts">
      <div class="fact"><h5>Data and source</h5><p>GA4 e-commerce reporting data from the course micro-assignments (Google Merchandise Store demo account).</p></div>
      <div class="fact"><h5>Target audience</h5><p>Digital marketing managers and e-commerce teams.</p></div>
      <div class="fact wide"><h5>Managerial problem</h5><p>The channels that bring the most sessions aren't always the ones that bring engaged visitors or revenue. Budget should follow value, not traffic.</p></div>
      <div class="fact wide"><h5>Research questions</h5><ul><li>Which channels drive the most engaged sessions, conversions and revenue?</li><li>How have revenue and engagement by channel changed over time?</li><li>Where do new and returning users differ?</li></ul></div>
      <div class="fact"><h5>Methods</h5><p>Descriptive statistics, percentage change, channel comparisons and a chi-square test on conversion rate by channel.</p></div>
      <div class="fact"><h5>Expected impact</h5><p>A clear case for prioritizing channels. Revenue attribution only where the data supports it.</p></div>
    </div>
    <p class="flow-label">Project workflow</p>
    <div class="flow">
      <div class="step"><b>Access</b><span>GA4 demo property</span></div>
      <div class="step"><b>Pull reports</b><span>Acquisition, engagement, monetization</span></div>
      <div class="step"><b>Compare</b><span>Rates and % change by channel</span></div>
      <div class="step"><b>Visualize</b><span>Bar and trend charts</span></div>
      <div class="step out"><b>Recommend</b><span>Channel priorities</span></div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Project page template {.proposal-panel}

```{=html}
<div class="wireframe">
```

## Color direction {.proposal-panel}

The ombré blends blush pink (`#F6CDE5`), lavender (`#C8B6EA`) and powder blue (`#BDDDED`). Deep purple (`#340963`) anchors headings and navigation. Berry pink (`#C52B83`) marks links, buttons and workflow arrows, and warm white (`#FCF9FD`) with charcoal (`#292332`) keeps text readable. The arched photo frame and the ✦ mark tie the site to my creative work.

## Reflection {.proposal-panel}

I want the portfolio to show both sides of how I work, the creative and the analytical. Building it pulls together what I've done across the program into something a hiring manager can scan in a few minutes. Tracking the site with GA4 also means the portfolio tests itself: I'll see which projects people actually open, and I can adjust from there.
